items.title: Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26887v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from conversational assistants into Cowork Agents capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and complex task execution. Financial analysis requires these agents to integrate cross-document evidence and perform multistep numerical reasoning, but expert task authoring is costly, while direct LLM synthesis struggles to produce challenging tasks with reliable answers. We introduce Navalia, a framework for Cowork Agents that combines verifiable task synthesis with long-horizon post-training. Using corporate financial reports as its data source, Navalia semantically selects supporting evidence from complete fact sets and constructs executable computation chains to generate analytical tasks with traceable evidence and actual data dependencies between steps. We further use independent LLM review and programmatic checks to verify evidence consistency and answer correctness. The verified tasks are then used for trajectory collection, cold-start supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL) to improve long-horizon task execution. Navalia, initialized from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, achieves consistent gains over the base model across all five benchmarks: OfficeQA Pro, FinSearchComp, Finance Agent Benchmark, APEX-Agents-AA, and Workspace-Bench-Lite. These results demonstrate that Navalia improves evidence integration, tool use, and long-horizon task execution capabilities and generalizes to broader Cowork settings, including general office tasks.

_analysis.title: Navalia：通过可验证任务合成与长程后训练推进协作智能体
_analysis.summary: Navalia 以企业财报为数据源，通过语义选取证据并构建可执行计算链，合成带可追溯证据与真实数据依赖的分析任务，再用独立 LLM 审核与程序化校验确保答案正确。验证后的任务用于轨迹采集、冷启动 SFT 与强化学习，基于 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 在五个基准上均优于基座模型，并泛化到通用办公场景。
_analysis.summary_en: Navalia synthesizes verifiable financial analysis tasks from corporate reports by semantically selecting evidence and building executable computation chains with traceable dependencies, then validates them via independent LLM review and programmatic checks. The verified tasks drive trajectory collection, cold-start SFT, and RL; initialized from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, it consistently outperforms the base model on five benchmarks and generalizes to broader cowork settings.

items.title: Large language model and reinforcement learning based autonomous construction and progress updates
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26899v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Due to the rapid growth of the global population, traditional construction methods are gradually unable to meet the current housing demand. The advancement of machine learning algorithms has encouraged researchers to explore their applications in the construction industry, leading to more intelligent and efficient building processes. In particular, the rise of large language models in recent years has provided more possibilities for the transformation from traditional construction to smart construction. In this study, a large language model and reinforcement learning based autonomous construction method is proposed. An enhanced soft actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm is developed to plan actions for a mobile crane according to construction tasks. Robot kinematics and control algorithms are used to ensure that the actions generated by the reinforcement learning algorithm can be executed by the crane. In addition, a customized embedding model is developed to extract information from the construction environment according to user interests. Then, a large language model, ChatGPT 5, is used to update construction progress, provide safety information to control system, and generate construction progress reports. The feasibility of proposed method is verified through several full-scall retaining wall construction experiments.

_analysis.title: 基于大语言模型与强化学习的自主施工与进度更新
_analysis.summary: 该研究提出一种基于大语言模型与强化学习的自主施工方法：用增强型软演员-评论家算法为移动起重机规划施工动作，结合机器人运动学与控制算法保证可执行性；定制嵌入模型按用户兴趣提取施工环境信息；再用ChatGPT 5更新施工进度、向控制系统提供安全信息并生成进度报告，并通过多项全尺寸挡土墙施工实验验证可行性。
_analysis.summary_en: This study proposes an autonomous construction method combining LLMs and reinforcement learning: an enhanced soft actor-critic algorithm plans mobile crane actions for construction tasks, with robot kinematics and control ensuring executability; a customized embedding model extracts environment information by user interest; ChatGPT 5 updates progress, supplies safety information to the control system, and generates progress reports. Feasibility is verified via full-scale retaining wall construction experiments.

items.title: Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26904v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent studies have proposed reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) methods that enable LLMs to generate high-quality RTL circuits from natural-language specifications. Existing approaches optimize circuit PPA (Power, Performance, Area) by aggregating multiple objectives into a single scalar reward, making it difficult to simultaneously generate diverse Pareto-optimal solutions across different trade-offs such as low power, low latency, and small area. However, in practical design, the relative importance of each objective varies depending on product requirements and design constraints; thus, obtaining a diverse and high-quality candidate set is beneficial in that designers can choose a preferred trade-off a posteriori. In this work, we are the first to propose a learning method for LLM-based circuit generation that optimizes, not the quality of a single circuit, but the quality and diversity of the entire circuit set obtained through multiple generations in the PPA objective space. The proposed method consists of (1) a generation-based training pipeline that reformulates coverage improvement of the entire Pareto solution set into a sequential circuit generation problem, and (2) a reward function based on Hypervolume Contribution (HVC) that measures how much a generated circuit contributes to the Pareto front. Evaluation on the RTLLM v2 benchmark shows that the proposed method achieves +13.3 percentage points in relative Hypervolume over a baseline without PPA optimization and +14.4 percentage points over a single-objective reinforcement learning method, while also demonstrating superiority in circuit diversity.

_analysis.title: 基于多目标强化学习与大语言模型的帕累托最优RTL代码生成
_analysis.summary: 该研究提出首个面向LLM电路生成的多目标强化学习方法，不再优化单个电路质量，而是优化多次生成所得电路集合在PPA目标空间中的质量与多样性。方法包含基于生成的训练流程，将帕累托解集覆盖率提升重构为序列电路生成问题，以及基于超体积贡献（HVC）的奖励函数。在RTLLM v2基准上，相对超体积较无PPA优化基线提升13.3个百分点，较单目标强化学习提升14.4个百分点，电路多样性亦更优。
_analysis.summary_en: This work proposes the first multi-objective RL method for LLM-based circuit generation that optimizes the quality and diversity of the entire generated circuit set in PPA space, rather than a single circuit. It uses a generation-based training pipeline reformulating Pareto-set coverage as sequential generation, plus a Hypervolume Contribution (HVC) reward. On RTLLM v2 it gains +13.3 pp relative Hypervolume over a no-PPA baseline and +14.4 pp over single-objective RL, with better diversity.

items.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26913v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models for radiology report structuring has been largely dominated by either proprietary cloud-based models or large open models requiring high-end GPUs for deployment, which is a critical bottleneck for clinical adoption in radiology workflows that demand data privacy and offline operation. To address this, we present MedPAO-Assist, an edge-deployable agentic framework that generates structured radiology reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, requiring only $\approx3.3$ GB peak RAM and achieving an average end-to-end latency of $\approx31$ seconds on a standard laptop CPU through an asynchronous, multi-threaded execution pipeline. The system currently supports four major imaging modalities -- Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. To our knowledge, it is among the earliest agentic systems to run its entire pipeline with a Small Language Model (SLM) in the 0.6B-parameter range. This multi-agent architecture, built around an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm, performs concept extraction, SNOMED-CT grounding, and structured report generation, followed by a speech-driven human-in-the-loop correction phase, together forming a fully "no-touch" reporting workflow that requires no keyboard input, external API calls, or internet connectivity. We evaluate each pipeline stage individually -- concept extraction, ontology grounding, and concept categorization and report hardware profiling results demonstrating the system's feasibility for real-time, CPU-only clinical deployment.

_analysis.title: MedPAO-Assist：可边缘部署、模态感知的放射报告结构化智能体AI
_analysis.summary: 提出MedPAO-Assist，一个可在边缘设备部署的多智能体框架，基于0.6B参数小模型，通过提取-对齐-生成范式，从放射科医生口述和语音指令直接生成结构化报告，仅需约3.3GB内存，笔记本CPU上端到端延迟约31秒，支持四种影像模态，全程无需键盘、外部API或联网。
_analysis.summary_en: MedPAO-Assist is an edge-deployable multi-agent framework using a 0.6B-parameter small language model to generate structured radiology reports from dictation and voice commands via an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm. It needs only ~3.3 GB RAM and ~31s end-to-end latency on a laptop CPU, supports four imaging modalities, and requires no keyboard, external API, or internet.

items.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26924v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: General-purpose agents are increasingly expected to perform professional analytics work, which requires sustained reasoning, iterative investigation, and reliable evidence. Training these capabilities requires diverse and challenging tasks. However, generating tasks directly from raw data often overlooks deeper questions that emerge through analysis and provides limited evidence for verification. To address these limitations, we introduce DataPraxis, an analytics task synthesis framework based on verified workspace evolution. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, then inherits and combines these workspaces to uncover deeper questions. It constructs tasks from accumulated findings and their dependencies, verifying analytical results both during evolution and after task assembly. Using this framework, we construct DataPraxis-5K, a dataset of 5,000 verified trajectories spanning diverse domains and output formats, to train DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B. DataPraxis-27B achieves 55.11 on DABStep and 51.9 on JobBench, matching or surpassing frontier models such as GLM-5.2. DataPraxis-5K is available at huggingface.co/datasets/stargazerhust/DataPraxis-5k

_analysis.title: DataPraxis：通过验证式工作区演化扩展分析任务
_analysis.summary: 提出DataPraxis分析任务合成框架，通过逐步丰富并继承验证过的工作区来生成更深层问题，构建了5000条验证轨迹数据集DataPraxis-5K，训练出的DataPraxis-27B在DABStep和JobBench上匹配或超越前沿模型。

It builds DataPraxis-5K, a 5,000-trajectory verified dataset, and trains DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B, with DataPraxis-27B scoring 55.11 on DABStep and 51.9 on JobBench, matching or surpassing frontier models like GLM-5.2.

items.title: H2DF: Calibrated Target Bands for Controllable Language-Model Unlearning
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26864v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gradient ascent (GA) is a simple language-model unlearning baseline, but it continues increasing forget loss after useful forgetting has occurred. This unbounded pressure can damage retained utility and make forgotten examples abnormally high-loss. We introduce H2DF, a calibrated target-band objective that applies GA-like pressure below a data-dependent lower target and suppresses, or reverses, that pressure after the target region is reached. The targets are estimated from matched non-member examples before training, so the base objective requires one forget-batch forward/backward pass per optimization step; our reported TOFU variant adds sparse retain replay every tenth step. We instantiate a one-sided objective for TOFU question answering and a two-sided objective for MUSE-News language modeling. Across three TOFU seeds, H2DF obtains a forget NLL of 1.528 with margin 0.049 and retain NLL of 1.165 with margin 0.047, matching GradDiff while using retain replay only every tenth step and showing substantially lower variability than GA. On MUSE-News, H2DF improves retention over GA and NPO and is competitive with SimNPO, but does not dominate it. Ablations show that the upper target reduces overshoot and that validation-based checkpoint selection is important. These results support calibrated target bands as a practical mechanism for controlling forgetting strength, while also exposing sensitivity to random seed and calibration quality.

_analysis.title: H2DF：用于可控语言模型遗忘的校准目标区间
_analysis.summary: 提出H2DF，一种校准目标区间目标函数，用于语言模型遗忘。它在数据相关下界以下施加类似梯度上升的压力，达到目标区间后抑制或反转该压力，从而控制遗忘强度、保护保留效用，并在TOFU和MUSE-News上验证效果。
_analysis.summary_en: H2DF introduces a calibrated target-band objective for language-model unlearning: it applies GA-like pressure below a data-dependent lower target and suppresses or reverses it once the target region is reached, controlling forgetting strength while preserving retained utility, validated on TOFU and MUSE-News.

items.title: AutoTerm-SST: Adaptive Terminology Memory with Zero Session-Time Setup for Streaming Speech Translation
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26865v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retrieval-augmented speech translation improves rare terminology, but systems such as RASST still assume that users provide a glossary before each session. That assumption is inconvenient for live talks, while merging every domain into one growing glossary eventually places too many irrelevant terms in the same retrieval and prompt competition. We present AutoTerm-SST, an interactive system that removes session-time glossary upload and domain selection. It organizes a large offline terminology catalog into topic slices, matches recent streaming translation context to bilingual slice prototypes, and activates a compact multi-slice working set under fixed retrieval and prompt budgets. On five ACL and five ESO oncology talks, AutoTerm matches a known-domain reference in terminology accuracy (88.3% vs. 88.1%) and mWER-resegmented BLEU (45.09 vs. 45.19), while requiring no domain input. Compared with a one-million-entry merged glossary, it improves terminology accuracy by 3.9 points and BLEU by 2.30. Routing plus four-slice retrieval remains lightweight: the complete system runs at 0.406 RTF, and the vLLM host sustains 32 real-time sessions. The live demo exposes active slices and retrieved terminology as the topic changes, providing zero-setup terminology-aware streaming translation.

_analysis.title: AutoTerm-SST：零会话配置的自适应术语记忆流式语音翻译系统
_analysis.summary: AutoTerm-SST 提出一种交互式流式语音翻译系统，无需用户在会话前上传术语表或选择领域。它将大规模离线术语库组织为主题切片，根据近期翻译上下文匹配双语切片原型，并在固定检索与提示预算下激活紧凑的多切片工作集。在 ACL 和 ESO 肿瘤学讲座上，其术语准确率与已知领域参考相当（88.3% vs 88.1%），相比百万条合并术语表提升术语准确率 3.9 个百分点、BLEU 2.30，系统整体运行达 0.406 RTF，vLLM 主机可支持 32 路实时会话。
_analysis.summary_en: AutoTerm-SST is an interactive streaming speech translation system that eliminates session-time glossary upload and domain selection. It organizes a large offline terminology catalog into topic slices, matches recent streaming context to bilingual slice prototypes, and activates a compact multi-slice working set under fixed retrieval and prompt budgets. On five ACL and five ESO oncology talks it matches a known-domain reference in terminology accuracy (88.3% vs 88.1%) and BLEU (45.09 vs 45.19) without domain input, while improving over a one-million-entry merged glossary by 3.9 points in terminology accuracy and 2.30 BLEU. The full system runs at 0.406 RTF, with the vLLM host sustaining 32 real-time sessions.

items.title: WaveCommitments: Private and Verifiable Speech-Agent Marketplaces
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26867v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern speech systems are evolving into ecosystems of autonomous speech agents that speak together, negotiate, and trade assets such as embeddings, spectrograms, or raw data. In such markets, sellers cannot reveal assets for evaluation due to privacy constraints, and buyers cannot price what they cannot test. Thus, we open-source WaveCommitments, an end-to-end design that pairs confidential asset valuation via Data Shapley inside a trusted execution environment with multivariate polynomial commitments. It enables selective openings and tamper-evident provenance to prove that a delivered asset matches the valuation while hiding everything else. Our extensive experiments across three known datasets and various tasks with state-of-the-art encoders, including Whisper, reveal that we speed up the best benchmarks by up to 20x while reducing their proof sizes by up to 39x. We also systematically study how a speaker's value shifts across tasks and encoders, revealing agent-level market prices.

_analysis.title: WaveCommitments：私密且可验证的语音智能体市场
_analysis.summary: 提出开源方案WaveCommitments，在可信执行环境内用Data Shapley进行保密资产估值，并结合多元多项式承诺实现选择性披露与防篡改溯源，使语音智能体市场中的卖方无需泄露资产即可证明交付物与估值一致；实验显示基准加速最高20倍、证明体积缩小最高39倍。
_analysis.summary_en: WaveCommitments is an open-source design pairing confidential asset valuation via Data Shapley in a trusted execution environment with multivariate polynomial commitments, enabling selective openings and tamper-evident provenance so speech-agent marketplace sellers can prove delivered assets match valuations without revealing them; experiments show up to 20x speedup and 39x smaller proofs.

items.title: Multimodal Ambivalence and Hesitancy Recognition with Bidirectional Audio--Text Cross-Attention
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26868v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ambivalence and hesitancy (A/H) are subtle behavioural states that can be expressed through both what a person says and how it is spoken. This paper presents an audio--text framework for video-level A/H recognition. Full-video transcripts and speech waveforms are encoded using pre-trained multilingual BERT and wav2vec~2.0, respectively, and projected into a shared representation space. Two stacked bidirectional cross-attention blocks allow linguistic tokens to attend to acoustic frames and acoustic frames to attend to linguistic context without requiring explicit temporal alignment. The resulting sequences are aggregated through masked mean pooling and combined using concatenation, element-wise products, and absolute differences for binary classification. We evaluate the model on the subject-independent split of the Behavioural Ambivalence/Hesitancy (BAH) dataset. The proposed system achieves 72.19\% accuracy, 75.00\% precision, 81.13\% recall, 77.95\% A/H F1-score, and 70.16\% Macro-F1 on the test set. These results demonstrate the potential of jointly modelling linguistic and acoustic information for automatic A/H recognition.code at:https://github.com/DorriG/ECCV.

_analysis.title: 多模态矛盾与犹豫识别：双向音文交叉注意力框架
_analysis.summary: 该论文提出一种音文多模态框架，用于视频级矛盾与犹豫（A/H）识别。使用多语言BERT和wav2vec 2.0分别编码文本与语音，通过双向交叉注意力实现无需显式时间对齐的跨模态融合，在BAH数据集上取得77.95%的A/H F1分数。
_analysis.summary_en: This paper presents an audio-text framework for video-level ambivalence and hesitancy (A/H) recognition. It encodes transcripts and speech with multilingual BERT and wav2vec 2.0, fuses them via stacked bidirectional cross-attention without explicit temporal alignment, and achieves 77.95% A/H F1 on the BAH dataset.

_article.title: 多模态矛盾与犹豫识别：双向音文交叉注意力框架

items.title: Mixture of Phonetic Experts Based Low-Rank Adaptation of Conformer Models for Accented English Speech Recognition
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26888v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Mixture of Phonetic Experts based Low-Rank Adaptation (MoPE-LoRA), a parameter-efficient adaptation framework for accented English speech recognition. Recent mixture-of-experts approaches typically allocate experts per accent, implicitly treating accent identity as the primary axis of variation. In contrast, we organize adaptation along phonetic categories, motivated by the observation that accent differences are often expressed as systematic distortions of phoneme realization. MoPE-LoRA introduces a fixed set of six low-rank experts aligned with manner-of-articulation classes and performs frame-level routing through a hybrid mechanism that combines phoneme supervision with learned acoustic gating. Because the expert set is shared across accents, the model does not require accent-specific modules and naturally extends to previously unseen accents. Experiments on L2-ARCTIC show that MoPE-LoRA consistently improves over single LoRA and full fine-tuning. In zero-shot evaluation where one accent is held out during training, the proposed method yields a 12.3% relative improvement over single LoRA. These results indicate that phonetic-category-based decomposition offers a scalable and transferable alternative to accent-level adaptation.
